_comment: `active` is the default backend for every agent; `agents.<agent>.backend` overrides it,
and the CODE_GRAPH_BACKEND env var overrides both. There is deliberately no
`active: "all"` — running every backend at once is a benchmarking concept only, and
kgbench composes its own per-arm MCP configs rather than going through this field.
There is also deliberately no query-type routing here. Which backend suits which kind of
question is what the benchmark exists to measure; encoding a guess now would bias it.
Adding a backend does NOT enable it. New backends ship with enabled:false and are
switched on only after scripts/backend-smoke.sh clears them.
The schema is enforced by validate() in lib/code-graph/registry.mjs, not by a
JSON Schema file — a second declaration of the same shape would only drift.
Run `node scripts/code-graph-config.mjs validate` to check this file.

graphify.summary: tree-sitter AST + semantic pass into a static graph.json, served over HTTP MCP

codegraph.summary: tree-sitter into SQLite/FTS5, served over stdio MCP

_toolsNote: codegraph_explore is the only tool exposed by default. The other seven
(node, search, callers, callees, impact, files, status) exist but are unlisted
unless CODEGRAPH_MCP_TOOLS names them. This list must mirror what the runtime
actually exposes — kgbench derives its --allowedTools from it, so any drift here
means the benchmark stops testing what production uses.

_envNote: NO_DAEMON/NO_WATCH make indexing deterministic — freshness is driven by the
reindex dispatcher, not by codegraph's own watcher or git hooks.
TELEMETRY=0 + DO_NOT_TRACK=1 are required: the container is keyless and must not

_mountNote: CODEGRAPH_DIR takes a plain directory NAME, not a path — absolute values are
rejected outright ('must be a plain directory name ... not absolute'), so the
index cannot simply be pointed at .data.
The repo is mounted read-only, and Docker cannot create a mountpoint on a
read-only parent, so `.codegraph/` must EXIST in the repo (tracked .gitkeep) for
the bind to attach. hostDir is then bound over mountPoint and every write lands
in .data. Verified end-to-end; see the Phase 0 spike.

index._indexNote: `codegraph init` ends with an interactive freshness prompt; run it with stdin closed or it hangs under supervisord.
